strengths: Rigorous theoretical framework connecting attention to entropic optimal transport with clear derivation that standard attention assumes uniform priors
Sophisticated mathematical results, particularly Theorem 2 proving SDPA-compatible shift-invariant priors must be finite trigonometric polynomials
Practical method elegantly disentangles positional structure from content via additive log-priors, addressing real problems like attention sinks
Comprehensive experiments across multiple domains (language modeling, long-context retrieval, DNA, vision) showing consistent improvements
True drop-in compatibility with FlashAttention without modification or overhead; well-designed for practical deployment
Theoretical justification of attention sinks as optimal transport defaults with stability analysis (Theorems 5.1, 5.4)
Novel connection between maximum-entropy principle and ALiBi-style recency priors (Theorem 3)
Demonstrates robust length extrapolation while maintaining in-distribution performance (1.55 point improvement over ALiBi on C4)
weaknesses: Practical improvements are modest and modest across tasks (1.55 perplexity on C4, small DNA improvements) without confidence intervals or statistical significance testing
Limited to small models (≤125M); scalability to large language models (1B+) unvalidated
Builds incrementally on very recent EOT interpretation of attention (Litman 2025); the core insight of generalizing priors, while elegant, is somewhat incremental
Key implementation details missing: exact MLP architecture for u(j), initialization schemes, sensitivity analysis across design choices
No ablation studies on critical hyperparameters like number of frequencies R, or comparison of different initialization strategies
Assumption F.3 (bounded learned prior) is theoretically motivated but practical necessity not justified; unclear when violating this would hurt
Vision experiments limited to ImageNet; 2D factorization is interesting but underdeveloped with no results on detection/segmentation tasks
Distinction between 'prior' and 'positional encoding' (Appendix E) is conceptually important but relegated to appendix rather than main text
Training computational overhead not quantified; throughput comparable to RoPE on DNA but more analysis needed for general applicability
Figure 2(c) showing signal strength vs. sink mass transition is intriguing but lacks analysis of why GOAT transitions smoothly while baselines do not

strengths: Novel EOT-based theoretical framework that elegantly interprets attention with learnable priors; Equation 5 cleanly captures the insight and is well-derived
Strong theoretical analysis of attention sinks with formal justification (Theorems 5.1 and 5.4) showing exponential suppression of context sensitivity vs linear for standard attention
Principled justification for parameterization: Theorem 2 rigorously establishes that SDPA-compatible translation-equivariant bounded priors must be finite trigonometric polynomials
Practical and efficient implementation within standard SDPA kernels without materializing dense matrices, maintaining full compatibility with FlashAttention
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple scales (125M, 1.23B) and diverse domains (NLP, vision, biology, multimodal) with careful ablations demonstrating robustness
Interpretable learned structures visible in figures (learned priors decompose into meaningful sink and relative components) and detailed appendices support reproducibility
weaknesses: Empirical improvements are modest and primarily for length extrapolation, not in-distribution performance; 1.23B results (Table 1) show GOAT matching RoPE in-distribution while practitioners already widely use RoPE, reducing motivation to switch

Incomplete computational analysis: no detailed wall-clock time/throughput comparisons despite claims of FlashAttention compatibility; pre-scaling trick requires careful engineering with unclear practical overhead

Limited vision and multimodal experiments: ImageNet shows only zero-shot resolution extrapolation (224→512px) without in-distribution accuracy curves; Spatial VQA confined to CIFAR-10 with gains difficult to contextualize

Theoretical results rely on limiting behavior (Theorem 5.1: ωi→0 dynamic range) and specific assumptions (Theorem 5.4: prior period not reached) that may not hold in practice with realistic head dimensions and sequence lengths

Dense presentation combining spectral decomposition, 2D extensions, sink parameterization, and scaling tricks obscures main insights; relationship between priors and positional encodings appears late (Appendix F)

Missing comparisons with recent attention variants beyond Shaw et al. and T5; no ablation isolating contributions of spectral vs sink components; DNA modeling improvements (27.0% vs 26.5%) are marginal

strengths: Novel EOT-based theoretical framework that reveals attention's implicit uniform prior and provides principled generalization via learnable priors (Propositions 2.2, 3.1)
Rigorous characterization of admissible prior classes (Theorem 2) justifying the Fourier parameterization under practical constraints (SDPA-compatibility, translation equivariance, stability)
Elegant algorithm design maintaining FlashAttention compatibility while factorizing position and content, with key-only sink parameterization that decouples structure from semantics
Formal first-principles explanation of attention sinks as optimal transport defaults (Theorems 5.1, 5.4) with quantified stability bounds, offering both theoretical insight and practical solution

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple scales and modalities (125M/1.23B language models, long-context retrieval, vision, biology, spatial reasoning) with thorough ablations and fair comparisons
Strong length extrapolation results (16× beyond training length on Passkey/NIAH, stable degradation at 1.23B scale) combined with in-distribution improvements (1.55 PPL over ALiBi)
Extensive reproducibility documentation with detailed hyperparameters, clear algorithm specification, and visualization of learned priors
weaknesses: Theorem 2's characterization that SDPA-compatible translation-equivariant bounded priors must be trigonometric polynomials is somewhat circular—the constraints were chosen to ensure SDPA-compatibility, so the result largely reflects imposed constraints rather than discovering fundamental structure

Empirical improvements vary: 1.55 PPL over ALiBi is solid but not dramatic; ImageNet results don't show in-distribution accuracy; DNA modeling is narrow; some ablations (Table 3) show diminishing returns with increasing Fourier modes

Incomplete analysis of critical design choices: initialization of sink MLP 'near zero' not ablated, numerical stability of √dh/dc scaling factor not analyzed, sensitivity to frequency base B only partially explored, training time overhead not reported
Limited baseline comparisons—only RoPE, ALiBi, and learnable PE included; missing recent alternatives (xPos, continuous position interpolation, other extrapolation schemes)

Presentation is dense with heavy theory (Sections 4, Appendix G); the connection between 'priors' and 'positional encodings' (Appendix F) could be introduced earlier; the scaling trick (Eqs. 23-27) is hard to parse

Evaluation gaps: no statistical significance testing or error bars; downstream task evaluation limited to synthetic long-context tasks (Passkey, NIAH); ImageNet vision results incomplete (only resolution extrapolation shown, not in-distribution accuracy)

Reproducibility concerns: MLP implementation details vague ('one-hidden-layer SiLU initialized near zero'—unclear hidden size and initialization scale), pre-scaling trick requires careful tuning with implementation gotchas not discussed, no mention of code availability
